chunks: The Commander of the Faithful, عليه السلام, said:

“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم entered upon a man from the descendants of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib while he was in the throes of death, and he had been turned away from the qiblah. He said: ‘Turn him toward the qiblah, for when you do that, the angels turn toward him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns toward him with His Face.’”
So he remained like that until he was taken.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the narrator of this report
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The direction of prayer toward which the dying person is to be turned
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: The angels who turn toward the dying person
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: A reverential formula for Allah meaning Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.يُقْبَضَ: To be taken, meaning to die or have the soul taken

ai.seo_question: Should a dying person be turned toward the qiblah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that the dying person should be directed toward the qiblah. It presents this act as one that brings angelic attendance and divine turning toward the person at the moment of death, showing the sanctity of proper conduct in a dying person’s final moments.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.349 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"The Messenger of Allah (sw) entered upon a man from the descendants of Abdul Muttalib, while he was in the throes of death and was facing away from the Qibla.
The Prophet said: 'Direct him toward the Qibla, for when you do so, the angels will approach him, and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, will turn toward him with His face (attention).'
And he remained in that state until he passed away.”
